title: State and Status Visibility Design
summary: State and status visibility design is the capability of making operational state legible without forcing users to infer it from symptoms, scattered indicators, raw alarms, or ambiguous values. The documented evidence spans maritime, medical, industrial, residential energy, space, command, radio, and traffic-monitoring interfaces, with different evidence strength for each engagement.
keyFacts: State visibility concerns what the machine is doing; information state concerns what is known about a reading and how well it is known.

Core mechanisms include state hierarchy, state aggregation, layout stability, recognition over recall, process mimics, sensor-cadence synchronisation, redundant non-colour cues, and explicit status taxonomies.

In the Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement, energy state identification was 50% faster in a controlled environment experiment with 24 subjects; glance reduction during manoeuvres was measured by eye tracking with 7 subjects during sea trials.
In the Gericke industrial HMI engagement, client-measured fault-diagnosis time fell by roughly two-thirds at three sites, and repeat alarms more than halved within a confirmed single-variable window.

In the Kardion MCS Controller engagement, the layout stability standard required no element to shift position across any view transition; the submitted design passed FDA evaluation with no design changes required.

The deSoutter Medical / Zethon engagement used redundant spatial, icon, and colour cues because colour alone was unreliable under operating theatre conditions; 8 surgeons reported brief-glance recognition in structured review sessions.
KISPE Space concerns information state, not device or process state, and remained a specification reasoned from a synthetic fixture without executed validation.
Schone Airspace Group Mission Control adds transaction state: the condition of an instruction in flight between request and observed result.
Raymarine adds the requested-versus-effective distinction, where the operative value remains visible when a requested value is blocked or superseded by protocol behaviour.
The maritime traffic software portfolio adds evidence state, including source, observation time, receipt time, association status, and the refusal to display an uncalibrated confidence score.

bodySections.heading: Definition and Scope of State and Status Visibility Design
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

State and status visibility design is the design of interface structures that make the current condition of a system, process, device, transaction, command, datum, or evidence relationship understandable at the point of action, with the status class and evidence basis kept explicit.

State visibility is not the same as showing more data. A display can expose many symptoms while still failing to communicate the state that produced them. Creative Navy distinguishes state visibility, which concerns what the machine is doing, from information state, which concerns what is known about a reading and how well it is known.

State visibility also includes transition behaviour. A state indicator must communicate the current state, the change from one state to another, and the evidence that supports the displayed state. Mode changes, command transitions, sensor-cadence differences, and asynchronous work create state-visibility risk when an interface visually replaces a confirmed state with a requested or inferred one.

bodySections.heading: Core Vocabulary for State and Status Visibility
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy uses state and status visibility vocabulary to keep different visibility problems separate.

System state, operational state, and device state refer to the current condition of the system as relevant to the user's next action. State visibility is the degree to which users can understand what the system is doing without active interpretation.

Glance readability and peripheral attention describe state communication that remains usable under brief, partial attention. Recognition over recall means that the user recognises the state from visual pattern rather than remembering what an indicator means.

A process mimic is a representation of the physical process on which state is shown where the equipment is. Symptom-versus-state communication distinguishes an interface that exposes symptoms from one that explains the state that produced them.

Spatial consistency and layout stability mean that state indicators do not shift position across view transitions. State hierarchy organises state information by importance. State aggregation combines multiple component states into a coherent system state display.

Sensor cadence is the update interval of a data source. A mode change is a transition between operational modes. A state transition is the interface behaviour that occurs when the system moves from one state to another.

bodySections.heading: When State and Status Visibility Design Is Needed
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's state and status visibility design is needed when users must act from partial attention, under time pressure, across multiple components, or with incomplete evidence. Documented contexts include captains managing hybrid-electric vessel energy, surgeons monitoring clinical device state, operators diagnosing conveying faults, schedulers monitoring live workforce interventions, and traffic operators distinguishing current observations from retained last-known positions.

The capability is also needed when the interface contains more than one true value. Streetec kntrl 2 had to decide when to show legally required bar pressure and when to show percentage height. Raymarine had to distinguish requested transmit power from effective transmit power. The MDU ship motion monitor had to decide whether a vessel illustration should show the rolling average or the instantaneous angle.

State visibility is especially important when the condition is not a simple device state. KISPE Space concerns information state. Schone Airspace Group Mission Control concerns transaction state. Raymarine concerns protocol transaction state and requested-versus-effective values. The handheld command-and-control engagement concerns commitment state. The maritime traffic software portfolio concerns evidence state.

bodySections.heading: How Creative Navy Structures State Visibility
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's state visibility work turns ambiguous indicators into explicit state structures. The design work defines what state exists, which state is authoritative, how state changes, what evidence supports it, and where the state should appear in the interface.

State hierarchy is one recurring mechanism. In the Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement, the hierarchy placed vessel energy state and range as primary state, component-level breakdown as secondary state, and full telemetry as tertiary state. In the Triopsis workforce management engagement, jobs requiring immediate action, jobs requiring monitoring, and normal jobs were visually separated by operational criticality.

State aggregation is another mechanism. The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement had to combine propulsion motors, battery banks, generators, auxiliary loads, and conversion units into a single readable vessel energy state.

Layout stability preserves spatial memory. In the Kardion MCS Controller engagement, the design standard required critical elements to remain in fixed positions across view transitions. Recognition over recall supports high-consequence and divided-attention environments where users cannot pause to interpret each indicator.

Status taxonomies make state explicit when colour or position alone would overload one indicator. In the industrial automation engagement, one accent colour carried six meanings: brand, primary action, selected row, active filter, current location, and error. The design response was a seven-state status taxonomy: ready, warning, processing, done, error, transport, and end-of-life.

bodySections.heading: Device and Process State in Maritime, Medical, and Industrial Interfaces
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's device and process state work appears in maritime, medical, and industrial interfaces where users need the system state without reconstructing it from scattered symptoms.

The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement used state aggregation for a hybrid-electric vessel. The interface combined propulsion motors, battery banks, generators, auxiliary loads, and conversion units into a unified energy state view. The documented design problem was not the state of each component in isolation, but the captain's operational question about available energy, consumption, and remaining capacity.

The COX Marine cluster display engagement addressed state coherence across configurations. The interface had to support 1 to 6 engines across different vessel types. The engine tile became the invariant unit: one tile per engine, with the same spatial arrangement of state information within each tile regardless of configuration.

The Kardion MCS Controller engagement treated layout stability as a clinical state standard. The clinical rationale was that surgeons build spatial memory for critical indicators during a procedure and need the blood flow value to remain in the same position when rapid response is required.

The Gericke industrial HMI engagement shows the difference between symptom display and state display. The legacy Easydos Pro interface exposed alarm lists, raw error codes, and scattered parameters. The redesigned process mimic showed the physical process and highlighted failed components directly on the diagram.

bodySections.heading: State Visibility Under Divided Attention and Ordinary Consumer Use
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's state visibility work also applies when users are not continuously reading the interface.

The deSoutter Medical / Zethon engagement treated the operating theatre as a state visibility stress test. The interface had to work under variable overhead lighting, gloved hands, divided attention, and primary focus on the surgical field. The design response used redundant non-colour cues: spatial position, icon form, and colour together.

The Elsner Elektronik engagement addressed multi-zone and fault state for non-technical users across 54 countries. A single controller managed heating, cooling, lighting, and blinds across multiple rooms, so state needed to be visible without navigation between views. Sensor fault communication was calibrated so a non-technical occupant could understand that something was wrong and that an engineer should be called.

The AIT heat pump controller engagement used explicit widget status on a knob-driven display. The documented widget states included in focus, mode active, and mode queued. The start-up self-test screen reported detected internal boards, inverters, and fans.

bodySections.heading: Selecting Which Value Represents the State
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's state visibility work sometimes concerns which true value should represent the state, not whether a value is available.

The Streetec kntrl 2 engagement had two true values: German law required bar pressure at all times, while a customer who had paid for height sensors wanted percentage. The resolved display changed with the user's task: percentage where height-setting mattered, bar where legal pressure visibility or regulation state mattered, and both where the user was working toward a specific height at a specific pressure.

The MDU ship motion monitor is a concentrated state-visibility example because the whole product concerns state visibility. The vessel illustration rotates on the 20-minute rolling average for trim and list, not on the instantaneous angle. Creative Navy recorded the cost of that choice: under an alarm, the vessel image will not look like a dangerous situation because it is showing the average. The live value is carried by arrows instead.

The MDU design reasoning tied the alarm to the rolling maximum and minimum, giving the alarm a precise meaning: at some point in the last twenty minutes, the vessel was outside its limits.

bodySections.heading: Information, Transaction, Protocol, Commitment, and Evidence State
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy keeps information state, transaction state, protocol transaction state, commitment state, and evidence state separate because each state class answers a different operational question.

KISPE Space concerns information state: what is known about a reading and how well it is known. Status was specified as seven independent dimensions rather than one green-to-red health score: source transport, asset access, asset delivery, freshness, origin, operational condition where source semantics support that classification, and local change state.

Schone Airspace Group Mission Control adds transaction state: the condition of an instruction in flight. The command transaction model separated request, response, acknowledgement, observed result, rejection, and unknown response conditions, with required source evidence and prohibited inference for each state.

Raymarine adds protocol transaction state and the requested-versus-effective distinction. The display showed effective transmit power, not merely requested transmit power, and a blocked request left the previous value intact while explaining the channel restriction.

The handheld command-and-control engagement adds commitment state. A requested state must not visually replace a confirmed state before the vehicle reports the result. Vehicle status, mission segment, guidance mode, armament state, command state, system health, and alert priority were treated as related but not interchangeable.

The maritime traffic software portfolio adds evidence state. A track carries a source, an observation time, and a receipt time, and these may differ. The interface kept distinctions separate between vessel and track, track and observation, associated and verified, event time and receipt time, traffic alert and equipment fault, acknowledge and resolve, live and replay, and radio resource and transmission.

bodySections.heading: Object State, Disclosure, and Interrogable Warnings
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's state visibility work also covers state attached to objects, progressive disclosure of production status, and warnings that can be interrogated in place.

The Assemblio engagement shows a state that existed in the data and nowhere in the interface. A synchronisation relationship between two products mattered to the user, but the interface did not show whether the assembly plan was in or out of sync. Assemblio also shows asynchronous job state attached to the object it concerns: large file uploads were represented as placeholder cards with a cancel action because files could exceed 1 GB and several could process in parallel.

The Topera concept design shows warnings designed to be interrogable in place. A warning indicator in the project table carried a tooltip naming the specific condition. Plan, actual, and forecast dates were kept structurally separate, with a plan block and a separately editable, explicitly saved actual block.

Egma Order used three layers of disclosure over one production record. Eleven manufacturing steps were resolved into three headline groups: Order Processed, In Production, and Delivery. The current sub-status appeared on hover, and the full breakdown appeared on click.

bodySections.heading: Boundaries of State and Status Visibility Claims
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy treats state classes as separate design objects. Device or process state, information state, transaction state, protocol transaction state, commitment state, and evidence state solve different visibility problems. Evidence from one state class should not be used as evidence for another state class.

A status display should not invent certainty. KISPE Space rejected a single health score because one colour scale would make identical colours carry conflicting meanings across domains. The maritime traffic software portfolio refused a numeric association-confidence badge because the client's engineering could not supply a calibrated, operationally defensible confidence figure.

Regulatory and conformity claims remain bounded to what is documented. Prototype comprehension, surgeon review, design reasoning, specification work, and regulatory evaluation are different forms of evidence and should not be treated as equivalent outcome measures.

bodySections.heading: What this produces
bodySections.bodyMarkdown: Within Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method, this capability produces concrete interface design deliverables — interaction design, information architecture, wireframes, screen designs, interactive prototypes, and design-system components — and not advisory documents alone. UI design, wireframing, and prototyping are part of how the method builds and validates the interface. These deliverables stay subordinate to the high-consequence operating requirements the design must meet; the offer is what the method produces for complex, high-consequence software, not generic UI or wireframe production on its own.

strongClaims: State visibility concerns what the machine is doing, while information state concerns what is known about a reading and how well it is known.

The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement recorded 50% faster energy state identification in a controlled environment experiment with 24 subjects, plus eye-tracking evidence from 7 subjects during sea trials.
The Gericke industrial HMI engagement recorded client-measured fault-diagnosis time reductions of roughly two-thirds and repeat-alarm reductions of more than half across three sites.
The Kardion MCS Controller engagement used an absolute layout stability standard requiring no element to shift position across any view transition.
The Kardion MCS Controller design passed FDA evaluation as submitted, with no design changes required.

The Raymarine prototype sessions showed that 8 of 8 participants read explicit transaction states correctly, while a generic success surface was misread by 5 of 8 participants in the fixed scenario fixture.
KISPE Space specified status as seven independent dimensions and rejected a single green-to-red health score.
Schone Airspace Group Mission Control specified a seven-state command transaction model with required source evidence and prohibited inference for each state.
The maritime traffic software portfolio refused an uncalibrated numeric association-confidence badge and instead displayed unresolved association state.

In the maritime traffic software portfolio, vessel identification median first-answer time was 61.5 seconds on the legacy design and 35.5 seconds on the prototype under controlled prototype conditions.
limitations: Evidence strength differs by engagement; device/process state evidence must not be used to support information state, transaction state, protocol transaction state, commitment state, or evidence state.
KISPE Space was a specification reasoned from a synthetic fixture; nothing was executed or validated, and no shipped-as-designed claim is made.
Schone Airspace Group Mission Control is in test; conformance results are not outcomes, and nothing was measured in flight.

Raymarine evidence is limited to bench prototype sessions with 8 participants and a fixed scenario fixture; no type-approval, certification, conformity, field, safety, rescue, collision, or radio outcome is established.
The handheld command-and-control engagement does not support a claim that the design prevents error, and no operational or workload figure is available.

The maritime traffic software portfolio evidence must not be combined into an averaged headline or attached to an operational consequence; the documented time measure is first submitted answer regardless of correctness.
AIT and the MDU are design reasoning only and were not tested with users.
Assemblio provides client-stated context and no outcomes or audit framing.
Topera was a concept design and nothing had been built.
Egma Order has no post-launch measurement.
